# Lemon Garlic Chicken & Quinoa

This vibrant, one-pan meal is designed for two people and is naturally gluten-free and dairy-free. By utilizing fresh lemon and garlic, we maximize flavor without the need for heavy sauces or dairy-based fats.

## Preparation & Ingredients

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Chicken_Quinoa_Salad.jpg/1200px-Chicken_Quinoa_Salad.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **Prep Time**: 10 minutes | **Cook Time**: 20 minutes
- **Main**: 2 skinless chicken breasts, 1 cup dry quinoa.
- **Produce**: 1/2 bunch curly kale (de-stemmed/chopped), 1 lemon, 2 garlic cloves (minced).
- **Pantry**: 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, black pepper.

## Cooking Instructions
- **Step 1**: Rinse quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer. In a small pot, combine quinoa with 2 cups of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
- **Step 2**: While quinoa cooks, season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and the zest of half the lemon. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
- **Step 3**: Sear chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove from skillet and let rest for 3 minutes.
- **Step 4**: In the same skillet, add remaining oil and minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds, then toss in the kale and a splash of water. Sauté until wilted (approx. 3 minutes).
- **Step 5**: Fluff the finished quinoa and stir in the juice of half the lemon. Slice the chicken and serve over a bed of quinoa and kale, garnishing with remaining lemon wedges.

## Nutritional Facts (Per Serving)

- **Protein**: 42g
- **Carbohydrates**: 52g
- **Fat**: 12g

Selecting the right framework is critical for a 5-person startup team. High-uncertainty environments require a balance between rapid iteration and structured execution to avoid technical debt and scope creep.

## Methodology Evaluation Matrix

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Scrum_process.svg/1200px-Scrum_process.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

Criteria | Scrum | Kanban | Waterfall
Initial Delivery | Medium (2-4 weeks) | High (Continuous) | Low (Months)
Flexibility | High (Per Sprint) | Very High (Immediate) | Very Low
Documentation | Moderate | Minimal | Extensive
Meetings | High (Daily + Ceremonies) | Low (As needed) | Low (Phase gates)

### Startup Recommendations
- **Scrum**: Best if you need to provide regular, predictable updates to stakeholders or investors. The structured sprints help a small team stay focused on a specific goal.
- **Kanban**: The ideal choice for high-uncertainty environments. It allows the team to pivot instantly as user feedback arrives, with the least amount of overhead.
- **Waterfall**: Not recommended for mobile apps or startups. The rigid structure and heavy documentation are ill-suited for products that require frequent pivots.

### Decision Insight
For a 5-person mobile app team, **Kanban** typically yields the highest productivity by minimizing "meeting fatigue" and allowing developers to focus on the highest-priority features in real-time. If your team requires more discipline to stay on track, **Scrum** is the better alternative.

# Windows 11 Battery Troubleshooting

Significant battery drain on a 2022 Dell XPS 13 is often caused by background indexing, outdated firmware, or high-power display settings.

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Dell_XPS_13_9310.jpg/1200px-Dell_XPS_13_9310.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

## Diagnostic Step-by-Step

- **Generate Battery Report**: Open Command Prompt as Admin and type `powercfg /batteryreport`. Open the resulting HTML file to check "Design Capacity" vs "Full Charge Capacity."
- **Identify Resource Hogs**: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), go to the 'Processes' tab, and sort by 'Power Usage' or 'CPU.'
- **Adjust Power Settings**: Set 'Power Mode' to 'Best Power Efficiency' in Settings > System > Power & Battery.
- **Disable Startup Apps**: Go to Settings > Apps > Startup and toggle off non-essential items like Teams or Spotify.

## Open-Source Telemetry Tools

- **BatteryInfoView**: Provides a detailed log of battery charge/discharge rates and health.
- **HWiNFO**: Deep hardware monitoring for real-time power draw (W) of the CPU and GPU.
- **PowerToys**: Includes utilities to manage awake-states and visualize system resource usage.

Suddenly, the world dissolved. He wasn't in Neo-Tokyo anymore; he was standing in the lobby of the Kurosawa Plaza, or at least, a nightmare version of it. The data from the heist was badly corrupted. The marble floors rippled like water, and the ceiling was a jagged mosaic of static. A corporate guard walked past, but his head was a spinning cube of purple light, his voice a distorted loop of white noise. 

Elias reached out with his prosthetic hand, fingers twitching as he manipulated the data-stream. He grabbed a floating shard of memory—a fragment of a conversation—and pulled. "There you are," Elias muttered, sweat beading on his brow. Behind the glitching security door, he saw it: a shadow that didn't belong to the recording. # 5GHz Connectivity Assessment
Frequent signal drops on the 5GHz band while 2.4GHz remains stable often indicate high local interference or aggressive DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection) channel switching in dense urban environments like Chicago.

## Technical Troubleshooting Guide
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Wireless Channel Selection**: Avoid 'Auto'. Manually set 5GHz to **Channel 36, 40, 44, or 48** to avoid DFS interruptions. In high-density areas, use a 40MHz or 80MHz bandwidth rather than 160MHz to increase stability.
- **Smart Connect**: **Disable** this feature. It often forces devices to swap bands prematurely, causing the drops you are experiencing. Assign unique SSIDs to each band (e.g., 'Home_2G' and 'Home_5G').
- **Advanced Settings**: Adjust the **Fragmentation Threshold** to **2304** and the **CTS/RTS Threshold** to **2307**. Lowering these slightly from the default 2346/2347 can improve performance in environments with heavy collision/interference.

## Physical Placement Optimization
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Elevated Positioning**: Place the router at least 3-5 feet off the ground, ideally on a shelf or mounted high on a wall.
- **Central Hub**: Move the unit to the center of the 1,200 sq ft apartment to minimize the number of walls the 5GHz signal must penetrate.
- **Distance from Obstructions**: Keep the router at least 2 feet away from large metal objects, mirrors, and appliances like microwaves.
- **Antenna Orientation**: Position the center antenna vertically and the two side antennas at a 45-degree angle for optimal multi-floor/room coverage.

Week 1: Foundations & Opportunity Cost
- Objectives: Define scarcity, explain trade-offs, and calculate opportunity cost.
- Activity: 'The Island Survival' simulation where students allocate limited resources.

Week 2: Supply and Demand Dynamics
- Objectives: Map equilibrium, identify shift factors, and analyze price ceilings.
- Activity: Classroom market simulation using 'trading pits' for a specific commodity.

Week 3: Consumer Theory & Utility
- Objectives: Explain diminishing marginal utility and derive budget constraints.

Week 4: Production Costs & Firm Behavior
- Objectives: Differentiate fixed/variable costs and identify profit-maximizing points.
- Activity: Building a 'Paper Airplane Factory' to analyze labor productivity.

Week 5: Market Structures (Competition vs Monopoly)

- Activity: 'Brand Wars' analysis of local fast-food chains and their pricing power.

Week 6: Market Failures & Externalities
- Objectives: Identify positive/negative externalities and discuss public goods.

# Moen Sleek Maintenance Guide
A leak at the handle base of a Moen Sleek pull-down faucet is typically caused by a worn-out 1255 Duralast cartridge. This is a straightforward DIY repair.

## DIY Repair Protocol
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Kitchen_faucet_repair.jpg/1200px-Kitchen_faucet_repair.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Step 1**: Shut off hot and cold water supply valves under the sink.
- **Step 2**: Use a **3/32" hex wrench** to loosen the set screw behind the handle and pull the handle off.
- **Step 3**: Unscrew the dome-shaped collar (shroud) by hand or using a cloth for grip.
- **Step 4**: Use an adjustable wrench to remove the brass cartridge nut.
- **Step 5**: Pull the old **Moen 1255 cartridge** straight up, clean the housing, and insert the new cartridge, aligning the tabs.
- **Step 6**: Reassemble the nut, collar, and handle, then restore water pressure.

Service | Parts/Labor Cost | Total | Savings
DIY Repair | $45 (Cartridge) + $15 (Tools) | $60 | $115

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/TP-Link_logo.svg/1200px-TP-Link_logo.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

### Prioritized Router Checklist
- **Disable Smart Connect**: This is the primary cause of 'Handshake' failures for devices like LIFX and Kasa which require a dedicated 2.4GHz signal.
- **Channel Width**: Set 2.4GHz to **20MHz** (not Auto/40MHz) to reduce interference in dense areas like London.
- **DHCP Reservation**: Assign static IPs to the Nest Cam and Kasa Plug via the 'Address Reservation' tab in TP-Link settings.
- **Security Mode**: Use **WPA2-PSK [AES]**. Many older IoT devices fail to authenticate with WPA3 or mixed modes.

### 2.4GHz Band Isolation Steps
1. Log into your Archer AX50 admin panel (usually `192.168.0.1`).
2. Navigate to **Advanced > Wireless > Wireless Settings**.
3. Uncheck **Smart Connect**.
4. Rename the 2.4GHz SSID (e.g., 'ReadingNook_IoT') and keep the 5GHz SSID as the original name for your laptops.
5. Connect all IoT devices to the new 2.4GHz SSID.

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/Europa-moon.jpg/1200px-Europa-moon.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg

The year was 2184, and the Jovian Research Station *Aethelgard* hung like a silver needle over the cracked, icy plains of Europa. Kaelen, the station’s lead structural engineer, stood on the observation deck, his breath hitching as he stared at the Great Red Spot. It was a swirling, crimson eye the size of two Earths, staring back through the vacuum. The storms of Jupiter were beautiful, but they were also a reminder of how small their outpost truly was.

*Tap. Tap-tap. Tap.*

Kaelen froze. It wasn't the rhythmic thrum of the life support or the hiss of the coolant lines. It was external. Metallic. Deliberate.

"Aura, run a structural diagnostic on Sector 4, exterior hull," Kaelen commanded, his voice tight.

"Diagnostic complete, Kaelen," the navigation computer replied, its voice a calm, synthesized alto. "Hull integrity is at 99.8%. No micro-meteoroid impacts detected. No pressure variances."

"Then what is that sound? Listen to the audio sensors on the outer skin."

*Tap. Tap-tap. Tap.*

"I hear it, Kaelen. It does not match the frequency of the station's rotating assembly. It is not an echo of the internal pumps."

"Is it a loose thermal tile?" Kaelen asked, walking toward the comms console.

"Negative. All tiles are secure. The sound is localized near the airlock of the deep-core drill assembly."

Kaelen felt a cold sweat prickle his neck. "Are there any other vessels in the vicinity? Any automated drones from the surface?"

"The surface scout is currently docked in Sector 1. There are no other signatures within 500 kilometers. However, the tapping is increasing in frequency. It is now 120 beats per minute."

Kaelen looked back at Jupiter. The giant planet seemed to pulse with the sound. He moved to the airlock monitor, switching the external camera to infrared. The screen showed nothing but the dark, frozen hull, yet the sound was now a frantic staccato, vibrating through the floorboards of the deck. It sounded like fingers—thousands of them—drumming against the steel.

"Aura, open the exterior floodlights."

"Floodlights active."

The darkness was banished, revealing the stark white surface of the station. There was nothing there. No debris, no creatures, no machines. But the tapping didn't stop. It grew louder, a deafening roar of rhythmic strikes that seemed to be coming from *inside* the metal itself.

"Kaelen," Aura whispered, a glitch in her vocal processor making her sound almost human. "The vibration is not on the hull. It is coming from the ice below us. Something is reaching up."

Kaelen watched the monitor as a single, hair-thin crack began to spiderweb across the reinforced glass of the observation port. The tapping stopped. In the silence that followed, a low, guttural vibration shook the station to its core, and a single, pale shadow eclipsed the Great Red Spot.

# InventorySync REST API Reference

## POST /v2/inventory/sync
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/JSON_vector_logo.svg/1200px-JSON_vector_logo.svg.png Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

Synchronize local warehouse stock levels with the global inventory system. This endpoint supports bulk updates for multiple SKUs within a single request.

### Request Parameters
Parameter | Type | Required | Description
--- | --- | --- | ---
warehouse_id | string | Yes | Unique identifier for the source warehouse.
items | array | Yes | List of item objects to synchronize.
items.sku | string | Yes | Stock Keeping Unit (Format: AAA-000-00).
items.quantity | integer | Yes | Current stock count (Non-negative).
timestamp | string | Yes | ISO 8601 formatted date-time.

### Implementation Example
```python
import requests
url = "https://api.example.com/v2/inventory/sync"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
data = {"warehouse_id": "WH-01", "items": [{"sku": "ABC-123-XY", "quantity": 50, "timestamp": "2023-10-27T10:00:00Z"}]}
response = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

## Troubleshooting & Error Codes

### Common HTTP Status Errors
- **401 Unauthorized**: Your Bearer token is missing, expired, or invalid. Refresh your OAuth2 credentials.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: You have exceeded the rate limit (100 calls/min). Implement an exponential backoff strategy.
- **400 Bad Request**: SKU format does not match the required regex pattern (AAA-000-00).

# PIIA Self-Review Guide for CA Developers

## Legal Compliance & IP Protection Checklist
This document provides a framework for reviewing your Proprietary Information and Inventions Agreement (PIIIA) following your resignation in San Francisco.

### California Legislative Updates (2023-2024)
- **SB 699**: Reinforces that non-compete agreements are unenforceable in California, regardless of where or when they were signed. Employers cannot sue to enforce them.
- **AB 1076**: Requires employers to notify employees (current and former hired after Jan 1, 2022) that any non-compete clauses in their contracts are void.
- **Action Item**: Verify if you received a formal notice regarding the voiding of non-compete clauses by Feb 14, 2024.

### Key Review Provisions
Category | Focus Area | Self-Review Question
--- | --- | ---
Prior Inventions | Disclosure List | Did you list your startup idea in 'Exhibit A' when you joined?
Non-Solicitation | Employees | Does the clause prevent you from *hiring* former colleagues?
Non-Solicitation | Customers | Does it restrict you from *contacting* specific enterprise clients?
Hardware | Return Log | Do you have a signed receipt for the return of your MacBook/Phone?
IP Ownership | Work-for-Hire | Was any startup code written on company time or devices?

## Clean Break & IP Integrity Steps
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/San_Francisco_City_Hall_at_Night.jpg/1200px-San_Francisco_City_Hall_at_Night.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

1. **Hardware Audit**: Factory reset all personal accounts from company devices. Ensure all physical assets are returned and documented by IT.
2. **Invention Disclosure**: Review your 'Prior Inventions' list. If your new startup relies on IP developed *before* your employment, ensure it was clearly excluded in your PIIA.
3. **Data Sanitization**: Confirm that no proprietary company data (customer lists, source code, strategy decks) remains on your personal cloud storage or local drives.

# Vehicle Diagnostic Report: 2017 Honda CR-V

## Symptom Analysis & Repair Estimates
This report addresses the steering wheel vibration and burning smell reported for your vehicle in Denver, CO.

### Likely Causes & Diagnostic Priorities
- **Vibrating Steering Wheel**: Most likely caused by **warped front brake rotors**. When rotors are uneven, the brake pads pulsate against them at high speeds, vibrating the steering rack.
- **Burning Smell**: Likely a **seized brake caliper** or a slow oil leak from the valve cover gasket onto the exhaust manifold. A seized caliper would also explain the vibration and excessive heat.

### Component Inspection & Cost Estimates
Component | Inspection Priority | Est. Parts Cost | Est. Labor (CO)
--- | --- | --- | ---
Front Brake Rotors | Critical | $120 - $180 | $150 - $200
Front Brake Pads | Critical | $50 - $80 | $100 - $150
Brake Calipers | High | $180 - $250 | $150 - $200
Valve Cover Gasket | Medium | $30 - $60 | $200 - $300

# Fall Harvest Sage & Squash Risotto

A comforting, seasonal main course that is naturally vegetarian and gluten-free. This recipe uses arborio rice and fresh fall produce to serve 6 people under 90 minutes.

## Shopping List & Cost Estimate
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Butternut_squash_2.jpg/1200px-Butternut_squash_2.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- 1 large Butternut Squash (~1.2kg): $4.50
- 500g Arborio Rice: $5.00
- 1.5L Vegetable Broth (GF): $4.00
- 1 bunch Fresh Sage: $2.50
- 100g Parmesan Cheese: $6.00
- 2 Shallots & 1 head Garlic: $2.00
- 200ml Dry White Wine: $8.00
- 100g Butter: $3.00
- **Total Estimated Cost**: $35.00 USD

## Step-by-Step Preparation

Step 1: Roast the Squash
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg
- Peel and cube squash into 2cm pieces.
- Toss with oil and salt; roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until tender.

Step 2: Sauté Aromatics
- Finely dice shallots and mince garlic.
- Sauté in a large pot with 50g butter until translucent (5 mins).

Step 3: Toast Rice & Deglaze
- Add 500g rice to the pot; stir for 2 mins until edges are clear.
- Pour in 200ml wine; stir until fully absorbed.

Step 4: Simmer Risotto
- Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
- Wait for absorption before adding more; continue for 20 mins.

Step 5: Finish & Garnish
- Stir in roasted squash, remaining butter, and grated parmesan.
- Fry sage leaves in a little oil until crisp and place on top.

# Laptop Decommissioning SOP

Standard Operating Procedure for the IT Department regarding the secure retirement and disposal of corporate computing assets.

## Phase 1: Data Sanitization (NIST 800-88)
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Clear**: Perform a software-based reset using built-in factory tools for standard SSDs.
- **Purge**: Use specialized erasure software (e.g., Blancco) for high-security drives to ensure no data recovery.
- **Destroy**: Physically shred drives that fail the software erasure process at a certified facility.

## Phase 2: Inspection & Grading

Grade | Physical Condition | Functional Status
A | Like-new; no visible scratches or dents. | 100% Functional
B | Minor wear; small scratches or scuffs. | Fully Functional
C | Significant wear; cracked casing or missing keys. | Functional / Parts Only
Scrap | Severe damage or hardware failure. | Non-functional

## Phase 3: Inventory & Storage
- **Logging**: Enter Serial Number, Asset Tag, Grade, and Wipe Status into the 'Decommissioned Assets' spreadsheet.
- **Storage**: Place Grade A/B units in anti-static bags and store in the locked IT Secure Room.
- **E-waste**: Consolidate non-functional units in the 'E-Waste Bin' for monthly pickup by a certified Toronto recycler.

## Device Processing Checklist
- [ ] Verify Asset Tag against current inventory database.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

# Brother HL-L2350DW USB Detection Fix

## 1. Check Device Manager Status
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Brother-HL-L2350DW-Printer.jpg/1200px-Brother-HL-L2350DW-Printer.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- Right-click the Start button and select Device Manager.
- Look for 'Other Devices' or 'Printers'. If you see 'USB Printing Support' with a yellow triangle, right-click it and select 'Uninstall device'.
- Unplug the USB cable, wait 5 seconds, and plug it back in to force Windows to re-identify the hardware.

## 2. Manual Driver Installation (.inf Method)
- Download the 'Full Driver & Software Package' from Brother and extract it (don't just run the exe).
- In Device Manager, right-click your printer and select 'Update driver' > 'Browse my computer for drivers'.
- Select 'Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer' > 'Have Disk'.
- Navigate to the extracted folder and find the .inf file (e.g., `brpo13a.inf`) to force the specific Brother driver association.

## 3. Print Spooler Service Reset
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Press `Win + R`, type `services.msc`, and hit Enter.
- Scroll down to 'Print Spooler'. Right-click it and select 'Stop'.
- Navigate to `C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS` and delete all files in the folder.
- Return to the Services window, right-click 'Print Spooler', and select 'Start'.

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Chicago_Skyline_Daytime.jpg/1200px-Chicago_Skyline_Daytime.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

Item | Focus Area | Critical Requirement
CAM Audit Rights | Calculation | Demand annual itemized statements and the right to audit landlord records within 90 days.
Square Footage | Rentable vs Usable | Verify the 'Loss Factor' (difference between usable and rentable) complies with BOMA standards.
Force Majeure | Business Interruption | Ensure language includes 'epidemics' or 'government orders' to allow rent abatement during closures.
Security Deposit | Return Timeline | Commercial leases in Chicago typically follow a 30-45 day return rule; must be explicitly stated.
Maintenance | Repair Obligations | Distinguish between HVAC 'repair' (tenant) and 'replacement' (landlord) under NNN terms.

## Key Jurisdictional Details
- **Usable vs Rentable**: Under Illinois law, 'Rentable' includes your share of common areas (lobbies, hallways). Ensure your 1,200 sq ft is accurately measured as 'Usable' to avoid overpaying for shared space.
- **Security Deposit**: Unlike residential properties, Chicago's RLTO does not apply to commercial leases; the return timeline is governed strictly by the written contract terms.
- **Force Majeure**: Standard Illinois clauses often exclude 'economic hardship.' Explicitly include 'public health emergencies' to protect against future lockdowns.

# Home Mesh Network Strategy

To eliminate the signal drop-off in your 2,500 sq ft home, the nodes must be placed to overcome the 'far corner' modem location. Since the modem is in the basement, the primary node will act as the anchor, while the remaining two nodes must be positioned centrally on the first and second floors to create a vertical 'signal spine' through the house.

## Node Placement & Configuration Guide
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/TP-Link_Deco_M5.jpg/1200px-TP-Link_Deco_M5.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

Node | Location | Purpose
Main Node | Basement (Modem) | Connects directly to the ISP modem; ensures basement coverage.
Satellite 1 | 1st Floor (Center) | Placed directly above the basement node to relay signal to the main living area.
Satellite 2 | 2nd Floor (Hallway) | Positioned near the master bedroom door to provide line-of-sight to the 1st-floor node.

## Initial Setup Checklist
- **Download App**: Install the TP-Link Deco app and create an account.
- **Power Cycle**: Turn off your modem for 30 seconds before connecting the first Deco unit.
- **Bluetooth On**: Ensure your phone's Bluetooth is enabled for the initial discovery phase.
- **Update Firmware**: Immediately check for and install firmware updates for all three nodes.
- **Optimization**: Use the 'Network Optimization' tool in the app to select the clearest channel.

## Feature Recommendations
- **Beamforming**: **ENABLE**. This helps the Deco focus signal toward specific devices, benefiting both your 2015 and 2023 hardware.
- **Fast Roaming (802.11r)**: **DISABLE**. While great for 2023 devices, many 2015-era devices (and older smart home tech) may experience connection drops or 'ping-ponging' between nodes when this is active.

## vCard 3.0 and QR Configuration
Use the following raw text to generate the QR code. This format ensures compatibility with iOS and Android address books.

### vCard 3.0 Data String

### QR Error Correction Levels
- **Level L (Low)**: Recovers ~7% of data. Best for clean, high-contrast digital displays.
- **Level M (Medium)**: Recovers ~15% of data. Standard for most commercial uses.
- **Level Q (Quartile)**: Recovers ~25% of data. Ideal for environments with potential smudging.
- **Level H (High)**: Recovers ~30% of data. Allows for heavy customization or damage.

### Printing Recommendation
For a **2cm x 2cm** print on **textured paper**, use **Level Q**. The extra error correction compensates for the ink bleed and surface irregularities inherent in textured stock without making the modules too small for mobile cameras to resolve.

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/San_Francisco_from_Twin_Peaks_September_2013_panorama.jpg/1200px-San_Francisco_from_Twin_Peaks_September_2013_panorama.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

## Essential Clauses and Legal Restrictions
This checklist ensures your Non-Disclosure Agreement for independent contractors aligns with California's strict labor and privacy statutes as of January 2024.

### Mandatory Legal Clauses
- **Definition of Confidential Information**: Explicitly list source code, trade secrets, and proprietary algorithms.
- **Exclusions from Confidentiality**: Standard carve-outs for information already in the public domain.
- **Obligations of the Receiving Party**: Requirements for the secure handling and non-use of code.
- **Term and Termination**: Duration of confidentiality (typically 2-5 years or perpetual for trade secrets).
- **Return of Materials**: Protocol for deleting local copies of source code upon project completion.
- **Injunctive Relief**: Right to seek a court order to stop unauthorized disclosures.

### California Legal Restrictions
- **Non-Compete Provisions**: Under **SB 699** and **AB 1076**, non-compete clauses are void and unenforceable in California, regardless of where the contract was signed.
- **Non-Solicitation**: Generally unenforceable regarding employees unless used to protect narrow trade secrets; non-solicitation of customers is also heavily restricted.
- **Whistleblower Protection**: Must include notice of immunity under the **Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA)** for reporting illegal activities.

High CPU usage from 'System Interrupts' typically indicates a hardware communication error or a driver conflict. Follow these steps to isolate the cause.

Step 1: Check Device Manager
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Right-click the Start button and select **Device Manager**.
- Look for any items with a yellow exclamation mark (!).

Step 2: Run System File Checker
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- Open **Command Prompt** as Administrator.
- Type `sfc /scannow` and press Enter to repair corrupted system files.
- Follow with `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` to ensure the Windows image is healthy.

Step 3: Perform a Clean Boot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Type `msconfig` in the Windows search bar.
- Under the **Services** tab, check 'Hide all Microsoft services' and then 'Disable all'.
- Restart to see if the CPU usage drops, confirming a third-party driver issue.

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Steampunk_City_Concept.jpg/1200px-Steampunk_City_Concept.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

## Underwater City Districts and Social Hierarchy
Located in the crushing depths of the Atlantic, Neptune's Forge is a marvel of 19th-century engineering and bioluminescent wonder.

### City Architecture and Districts
- **Architecture**: Pressurized brass hulls reinforced with interlocking rivets and massive panes of bioluminescent 'Deep-Glass' that pulse with soft blue light.
- **The Deep Vents (Industrial)**: The city's foundation, where geothermal energy is harvested amidst soot-stained pipes and heavy steam machinery.
- **The Coral Gardens (Residential)**: A middle-tier district featuring hanging apartments integrated into giant, genetically hardened reef structures.
- **The High Pressure Plaza (Governance)**: The uppermost spire, encased in the thickest glass, where the elite oversee city operations far above the mud.

### Social Hierarchy: Oxygen Credits
Citizens earn 'Oxygen Credits' through labor, which dictate their breathing allowance and district access. To run low is to be relegated to the 'Thin-Air Slums' near the exhaust vents.

### The Rupture of 1924
A historical catastrophe where a primary pressure seal in the Vents failed, flooding 15% of the lower city and leading to the current strict credit system.

## Narrative Prologue: The Leaking Hulls
The brass hummed, a low thrum that resonated through the soles of Elias’s lead-weighted boots. Outside the thick viewport of the maintenance tunnel, the Atlantic was an infinite, ink-black void, save for the rhythmic pulse of the bioluminescent glass that kept the crushing weight of the ocean at bay. He was a 'Breather'—a diver whose life was measured in the steady hiss of the regulator and the dwindling balance on his credit-gauge.

He saw it first as a shimmer in the darkness. A hairline fracture in the brass plating of Section 4-G, just below the Coral Gardens. It wasn’t the jagged crack of a pressure fatigue; it was a series of deep, rhythmic gouges, as if something with teeth made of diamond had tried to peel back the city’s skin. A jet of freezing, high-pressure water hissed through the gap, a needle of ice in the humid steam of the tunnel. Elias reached for his welding torch, but his hand froze. From the gloom beyond the glass, a massive, unblinking eye—larger than a submersible—slid into view. It wasn't the machinery failing; something was trying to get in.

# Signal Optimization Strategy
Improving connectivity in a 2,500 sq ft home requires addressing both physical barriers and electronic interference.

## Technical Configuration & Upgrades
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Wireless_Router_with_Antennas.jpg/1200px-Wireless_Router_with_Antennas.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

1. Physical Placement Adjustments
- Centralize the Router: Move it from the corner to a more central location on the ground floor to reduce signal loss through exterior walls.
- Elevate the Device: Place the router on a high shelf or mantel; signal propagation is better when not blocked by furniture at floor level.
- Clear Obstructions: Ensure it is not inside a cabinet or near large metal objects (fridges) or masonry walls.

2. Router Settings Optimization
- Access: Login to `192.168.1.1` via browser using admin credentials.
- Channel Selection: Switch 5GHz from 'Auto' to a DFS channel (like 100-140) if available to avoid neighbor interference.
- Channel Width: Change 5GHz width to 80MHz for higher speed, or 40MHz for better stability and range to the second floor.

3. Hardware Upgrade Recommendation
- Recommendation: **TP-Link Deco X55 Mesh System (3-Pack)**.
- Price: ~$190 - $230 USD.
- Effectiveness: Placing one node on the ground floor and another directly above it on the second floor will create a seamless 'roaming' network that covers the entire 2,500 sq ft area.

# Windows 11 Performance Recovery Guide

This guide addresses the high CPU usage and lag on your Dell XPS 13 following the May 15th update. Follow these steps in order to restore system responsiveness.

## Immediate System Health Checks
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Dell_XPS_13_9310.jpg/1200px-Dell_XPS_13_9310.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Task Manager Check**: Press `Ctrl+Shift+Esc`. Click **Processes** and sort by **CPU**. Identify if 'Windows Update' or a specific browser is the culprit.
- **Startup Cleanup**: In Task Manager, go to the **Startup apps** tab. Disable high-impact apps like Spotify, Teams, or Cortana.
- **Command Repair**: Right-click Start, select **Terminal (Admin)**. Type `sfc /scannow` and press Enter to fix corrupted system files.

## Optimization and Service Management
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- **Background Services**: Search for 'Services'. Find **SysMain** (formerly Superfetch), right-click it, select **Properties**, and set Startup Type to **Disabled**.
- **Update Rollback**: If lag persists, go to **Settings > Windows Update > Update history > Uninstall updates** and remove the May 15th patch.
- **Power Plan**: Go to **Control Panel > Power Options**. Ensure **Balanced** or **High Performance** is selected to prevent CPU throttling.
